text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel, Finance Minister Dan Meridor compromise on multi-year inflation goal. Disagreement on target for 2001.
- National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon urges building of "Treasure Islands".
- New Tel Aviv-Jerusalem rail route gets initial okay.
- Ministry of Health: Sick fund deficit to hit 2.2 billion shekels in 1997.
- Trade and Industry Minister Natan Sharansky: Investment aid funds nearly used up.
- El Al airlines denies plans to fire top brass.
- Four companies seek to raise $20 million on London's Alternative Investment Market (AIM).
- Lack of trust, not details, block Hebron deal.
- Palestinian preventive security chief Jibril Rajoub: Israel can forget about asking Palestinian Authority to extradite PFLP killers.
- B'Tselem: Israel strip-searching Palestinian women in Hebron.
- Uri Geller, at 50, opens UFO conference in Israel.
HAARETZ
- Two attacks on Syrian targets in Lebanon, the first since the end of the civil war.
- United States: If the settlements are halted -- the dispute with Israel will also end.
- Assessment: Laser system to intercept Katyushas could be stationed on northern border in 1998.
- Religious affairs ministry transfers 78 million shekels from yeshiva seminary budget to religious middle schools.
GLOBES
- Budget assessment: Change in taxation levels will take place of planned higher doctor fees.
- Turkish consul in Tel Aviv: Casinos will be closed only to Turks and not to tourists.
- Building contractors: Slowdown to worsen during 1997; expectation of 5 percent drop in construction starts.
MAARIV
- Killers of mother and son from Beit El jailed for life in Jericho. Palestinians: They'll never be extradited.
- Jerusalem steadfastly denies Tehran accusation it delaying negotiations in matter of Ron Arad.
- New budget updated: Tax revenues will drop by 2.7 billion shekels largely because of slowdown in economy and real estate.
- American banks consider marketing mortgages in Israel.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- American threat: If the settlements are expanded, we'll cancel the loan guarantees. United States uses satellites to follow building activity in the territories.
($1 = 3.28 shekels)
